judged_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gates the feature on only CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, omitting the sibling flag CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT that refreshOAuthTokens additionally requires, leaving two inconsistent definitions of "enabled" on the same touched credential path. A self-hoster who sets the webhook secret and encryption key but not (or mis-spells) the sync endpoint gets the webhook endpoint active (accepting and overwriting credentials for any user id) while token refresh silently falls back to the provider endpoint — i.e., the feature appears enabled in one half of the path and disabled in the other, with no validation or error telling the operator which flag is missing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different “enabled” checks for the same overall credential-sync feature path. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined only as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts). The new webhook endpoint `/api/webhook/app-credential` uses only that flag (plus the header secret match) to allow credential writes, and does not require `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Meanwhile `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` to take the sync-path; otherwise it silently falls back to the provider refresh logic. This inconsistency is grounded in the diff and could confuse operators / lead to partially enabled behavior without validation. The claim that the webhook endpoint will accept updates for any `userId` is also true given a correct secret header, though it’s gated by the shared secret.
